Bambi is a high-level Bayesian model-building interface written in Python.
It works with the [PyMC](https://www.pymc.io/) probabilistic programming framework and is
designed to make it extremely easy to fit Bayesian mixed-effects models common in biology,
social sciences and other disciplines.

## Installation

Run these commands in an active Python environment.

### Released version

::: {.panel-tabset group="installer"}

#### pip

```bash
pip install bambi
```

#### conda

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge bambi
```

#### uv

```bash
uv pip install bambi
```

:::

### GitHub version

Install the development version directly from GitHub:

::: {.panel-tabset group="installer"}

#### pip

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/bambinos/bambi.git
```

#### conda

Use pip inside your active conda environment:

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge pip
python -m pip install git+https://github.com/bambinos/bambi.git
```

#### uv

```bash
uv pip install git+https://github.com/bambinos/bambi.git
```

:::

### Distribution of adoption times

Fit an exponential survival model for black cats and other cats, treating outcomes other than adoption as right-censored. The histograms show the posterior distributions of the mean adoption times in days.

{{< embed notebooks/homepage_examples.ipynb#adoption-model echo=true >}}

{{< embed notebooks/homepage_examples.ipynb#adoption-times echo=true >}}

For the full analyses, see [Sleepstudy](notebooks/sleepstudy.ipynb) and
[Survival models](notebooks/survival_model.ipynb). More examples are available in the
[gallery](notebooks/index.qmd).
